c47c56f63583.t: The Twelve Traditions and Twelve Concepts for World Service — the framework that keeps AA alive and autonomous.

d89c0de2a001.t: The Traditions are AA's home group rules — the principles that protect the fellowship's unity and independence. Written by Bill W. and adopted in 1950.

c5440356ebfa.t: <0>Our common welfare should come first;</0> personal recovery depends upon A.A. unity.

95ea3eb4fba0.t: <0>For our group purpose there is but one ultimate authority</0> — a loving God as He may express Himself in our group conscience. Our leaders are but trusted servants; they do not govern.

0e30b8a4b191.t: <0>The only requirement for A.A. membership</0> is a desire to stop drinking.

641484d043f5.t: <0>Each group should be autonomous</0> except in matters affecting other groups or A.A. as a whole.

c8d53aacc2e5.t: <0>Each group has but one primary purpose</0> — to carry its message to the alcoholic who still suffers.

0e55224b8f67.t: <0>An A.A. group ought never endorse, finance, or lend the A.A. name</0> to any related facility or outside enterprise, lest problems of money, property, and prestige divert us from our primary purpose.

820708f4a612.t: <0>Every A.A. group ought to be fully self-supporting,</0> declining outside contributions.

091e5615ccc5.t: <0>Alcoholics Anonymous should remain forever nonprofessional,</0> but our service centers may employ special workers.

4cb698cdf70e.t: <0>A.A., as such, ought never be organized;</0> but we may create service boards or committees directly responsible to those they serve.

5e3353f9c9b6.t: <0>Alcoholics Anonymous has no opinion on outside issues;</0> hence the A.A. name ought never be drawn into public controversy.

096b9362e4f7.t: <0>Our public relations policy is based on attraction rather than promotion;</0> we need always maintain personal anonymity at the level of press, radio, and films.

26d1893a822f.t: <0>Anonymity is the spiritual foundation of all our traditions,</0> ever reminding us to place principles before personalities.

2cf97da69a36.t: The Concepts describe how AA's world service structure operates — from the group conscience to the General Service Board. Written by Bill W. in 1962.

e32af397e692.t: Final responsibility and ultimate authority for A.A. world services should always reside in the collective conscience of our whole Fellowship.

b084094d334e.t: The General Service Conference of A.A. has become, for nearly every practical purpose, the active voice and the effective conscience of our whole Society in its world affairs.

e99705658413.t: To insure effective leadership, we should endow each element of A.A. — the Conference, the General Service Board and its service corporations, staffs, committees and executives — with a traditional "Right of Decision."

fc17395e8bba.t: At all responsible levels, we ought to maintain a traditional "Right of Participation," allowing a voting representation in reasonable proportion to the responsibility that each must discharge.

7b6164ceea73.t: Throughout our structure, a traditional "Right of Appeal" ought to prevail, so that minority opinion will be heard and personal grievances receive careful consideration.

6e113351c5ee.t: The Conference recognizes that the chief initiative and active responsibility in most world service matters should be exercised by the trustee members of the Conference acting as the General Service Board.

fa8e60e92af1.t: The Charter and Bylaws of the General Service Board are legal instruments, empowering the trustees to manage and conduct world service affairs.

a333fcb97375.t: The trustees are the principal planners and administrators of overall policy and finance.

c7a95ff21a1f.t: Good service leadership at all levels is indispensable for our future functioning and safety.

1ea61b4f0d4a.t: Every service responsibility should be matched by an equal service authority.

8d73b18df62b.t: The trustees should always have the best possible committees, corporate service directors, executives, staffs, and consultants.

a1c750b3e6c8.t: The Conference shall observe the spirit of A.A. tradition, taking great care that it never becomes the seat of perilous wealth or power.

c61d5bb10379.t: Anything else <0>Wheelchair access, which door, “closed meeting”, or that one of ours has closed or moved.</0>

e2b37d35d487.t: Founded 1935 in Akron, Ohio by Bill W. and Dr. Bob. The original 12-step mutual-aid fellowship for anyone with a desire to stop drinking. Peer support, anonymity, sponsorship, and the Big Book. Over 2 million members in 180+ countries.

5a87f94db7f0.t: Founded 1953. A 12-step fellowship for people recovering from drug addiction — any substance, any compulsion. Open and closed meetings worldwide with peer sharing and sponsor relationships.

083b8db255b1.t: Founded 1994. 12-step fellowship focused specifically on crystal methamphetamine recovery. Promotes total abstinence and connects those with a shared experience of meth addiction. Specialized focus helps members feel understood.

799ad000ed08.t: Started November 18, 1982 in Los Angeles. A 12-step program modeled after AA for anyone seeking recovery from cocaine and other mind-altering substances. Focused peer support for stimulant-related addiction.

719ee9751d38.t: Founded 1957 in Los Angeles by members of AA. A 12-step mutual-aid fellowship for compulsive gambling. Membership requires only a desire to stop gambling. Free, no affiliation — peer support and a structured recovery path.

20e02267f6dd.t: Founded 1977 in Minneapolis. A 12-step fellowship for individuals struggling with compulsive sexual behaviors. Grounded in AA principles with confidential peer-led meetings and structured recovery support.

2fb2853a11e4.t: Established 2019. Buddhist-inspired, peer-led recovery using mindfulness, meditation, and Dharma principles. Open to anyone — substances or process addictions. Compassionate, non-dogmatic framework rooted in self-awareness.

34a0bb58b569.t: Self-Management and Recovery Training. Secular, evidence-based alternative using CBT, REBT, and motivational tools. Structured workshops emphasizing self-empowerment and choice. Open to all forms of addiction.

250693bb3337.t: Christ-centered, 12-step recovery program for anyone struggling with hurt, pain, or addiction of any kind. Safe, supportive community finding freedom, healing, and hope through spiritual growth and practical steps.
